Hi Neha / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Helix legal circulated the draft order form and we have a couple of questions on the security exhibit before final sign-off. Attached is our SOC 2 summary for context (low-risk items called out).

High-level asks from InfoSec:
- Clarify the audit access language: they want to confirm whether the request can be scoped to the account and SOC2 assertions vs. broad "inspection rights."
- Pen test: they expect to run a vendor-led assessment. They asked whether Redwood requires a staging-only window (they prefer production with mitigation controls).
- Evidence cadence: they'd like to see an explicit list of deliverables (sample logs, config snapshots, pen test plan) and a weekly touchpoint during evidence collection.

Can you confirm what Redwood can agree to here and any required redlines to the MSA / Appendix? Procurement would also like to get the order form sent to DocuSign this week.

Amanda Chen
Senior Procurement Manager — Helix Health

Amanda — thanks for the context and the SOC2 summary. I've reviewed the items and sketched out a working approach below so we can be explicit for procurement and legal.

Proposed items Redwood can accept (draft language suggestions inline):
1) Audit scope: "Customer may request inspections or evidence limited to the Account's production resources and the SOC2-related controls applicable to the Services, subject to reasonable notice and coordination. Redwood will not be obligated to provide inspection access that materially risks other customers' data or shared infrastructure."
2) Notice window: we propose a standard 60-day notice for on-site or intrusive testing and a 10-business-day notice for evidence requests that can be satisfied via artifacts/exports.
3) Pen test staging: Redwood requires any active penetration test against production to be run against a customer-dedicated staging environment or under a jointly agreed plan that includes a mitigation and rollback protocol. We can accept vendor-led assessments with prior scoping call and test plan; only non-destructive testing will be permitted without a longer notice period.
4) Evidence cadence: propose weekly sprint check-ins (30 min) and a deliverable list: sample application logs (48–72 hour slices), access logs, configuration snapshots (redacted), and pen test plan + final report.

Next steps I suggest: Karthik to provide exact MSA/App A redline text and Laura to confirm legal's DocuSign timing. If this matches Helix's expectations I can prepare a one-page Mutual Action Plan and link it to DocuSign.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal Ops — Redwood Inference

Neha / Amanda — quick technical/legal redline summary from our side. Attached is a tracked changes file (redlines.docx) but the key points below so we can get to DocuSign quickly: 

- Move audit rights to Appendix A (Assurance Exhibit) and limit to "scoped inspections tied to SOC2/ISO attestations for the Services in-scope for the Account." This prevents open-ended inspection language in the MSA body.
- Replace "reasonable notice" with explicit windows: 60 days for active testing requiring escalated controls (e.g., simulated DDoS, exploit chain testing); 10 business days for log/config artifact requests. 
- Prohibit live intrusive testing on shared multi-tenant infra. If Helix requires live testing, it must be conducted in a customer-isolated environment that mirrors production.
- Evidence delivery format: prefer S3 export or encrypted Drive share. For any log samples, we will redact PII and only provide sample slices (we propose a maximum of three non-contiguous 24-hour slices unless a narrower scope is agreed).

If Helix can confirm the staging requirement and DocuSign timing we can accept and circulate a clean order form + Appendix A.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redlines.docx

Amanda / Brian / procurement,

Thanks for the quick replies and for being flexible on the mechanics. Per the thread and Karthik's redlines, I've created a short Mutual Action Plan (linked below) and attached a PDF that summarizes the agreed items so procurement can proceed to DocuSign. Summary of agreed points: 

1) Assurance Exhibit (Appendix A): audit rights language moved to Appendix A and limited to the Account in-scope controls tied to SOC2 attestations.
2) Notice windows: 60 days required for active penetration testing that could be intrusive; 10 business days for artifact/log requests exported via S3/Drive.
3) Pen testing: Redwood requires a staging-based execution or a jointly scoped production plan that includes a signed mitigation & rollback protocol. Redwood will provide a template mitigation plan during the scoping call.
4) Evidence cadence & deliverables: weekly 30-min check-ins during collection; deliverables to be S3 export or encrypted Drive share. Sample slices limited to three non-contiguous 24-hour windows, redacted per Redwood's PII rules.
5) Delivery format & redaction: Redwood will redact PII and provide guidance; any forensic requests that exceed the sample windows will require separate written agreement.
